title: Pattern 11
statement:

peerSolutions.title: Building alternating rows in Python
peerSolutions.author: Chirag Khanna
peerSolutions.content:
This version creates each row as a small list and prints it after filling the row. The starting number is chosen from the row number, so odd rows begin with `1` and even rows begin with `0`.

For example, row 3 is built as `[1, 0, 1]`, then converted to one space-separated line.

```python
class Solution:
    def pattern11(self, n):
        for row in range(1, n + 1):
            values = []
            start = 1 if row % 2 == 1 else 0

            for col in range(row):
                values.append(str(start))
                start = 1 - start

            print(" ".join(values))
```

Time complexity: `O(n^2)` for creating and printing the rows.
Space complexity: `O(n)` for the largest temporary row.
